assessment: The incumbent supports the required CSV workflow and appears useful under stable assignments: those 24 files had seven-minute median handling. Overall course-set accuracy was 80%, below 95%, and handling was 17 minutes, above 12. Assignment changes occurred in six affected exports, supporting investigation of temporal selection without establishing causation. The two renamed-course cases limit an assignment-only account: selection or human recognition could also fail. Zero observed cross-center rows is limited evidence because the split-course center was absent. Fast execution and slow replacement delivery suggest a separate service delay, not necessarily the source of measured handling time.

openings.claim: Current assignment or course-name interpretation may diverge from the intended historical week, while stable cases remain easy to use.
openings.delta: Distinguish incorrect export membership from correct membership that coordinators cannot recognize after a rename.
openings.prediction: With an agreed intended course set held fixed, changing only current assignment or display name will either change exported membership or change coordinator recognition despite identical membership.
openings.probe: Use fabricated staging cases for midweek reassignment and rename. Compare exported membership before and after each change, then ask consenting coordinators to identify included courses. Treat disagreement over the intended set as unresolved timetable semantics.
assumptions: Staging can reproduce the relevant selection behavior.
Existing identifiers or fabricated fixtures allow membership comparison without altering the documented CSV schema.

openings.claim: Does excess active handling arise mainly from course checking and correction, replacement requests, or spreadsheet importing?
openings.delta: Separate coordinator effort from replacement elapsed time before selecting the bounded intervention.
openings.prediction: A replacement-access intervention would reduce median handling only if requesting and following up consumes substantial active time; long passive waits alone would not support that prediction.
openings.probe: In the two short sessions, have six coordinators process fabricated unchanged and changed-course files in authorized workspaces. Time checking, correction, downloading, importing, and requesting separately; record passive waits separately. Use the results to bound a change within six engineer-days and existing hosting.
assumptions: Fabricated tasks approximate ordinary handling sufficiently to prioritize further work.
Sessions require no interruption of live attendance entry or external processing of participant names.
